Recommend removing `done:true` from the step frame or gating final done detection by presence of `provider`/`session_id`.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix path-mangling / business_voice_filter to bypass file paths matching well-known patterns (extensions .py/.js/.ts/.md, path segments containing '/' or '.agent/'). Its .agent→that/a project, repo→website, filename→page substitutions destroy the very file path the required_read_gate is inserting.

CRITICAL: Investigate why enforce_required_read_gate() fires only ~1/3 of the time on chat/stream. Possibilities: (a) state.required_read_gate stashed in worker.py isn't populated in some race (worker runs async, stream.py reads state before stash completes), (b) the pre-LLM classifier is non-deterministic and only sometimes tags this prompt with required_read_gate, (c) the enforcement is being placed after a code path that early-returns to the token-streaming loop with the original LLM content when gate metadata is missing.

CRITICAL REGRESSION: chat/send B3 gate no longer clean after this round's stream-side fix — the stream fix appears to have re-broken send (or send was already flaky and only appeared clean in round 2). Re-audit send path too.
MINOR: Change intermediate SSE step frame to not carry `done:true` (currently `{type:step, text:'✅ Done', done:true}` collides with the terminal done event and confuses SSE consumers).

Consider making required_read_gate enforcement idempotent: after enforce_required_read_gate() rewrites the text, freeze it in state and have business_voice_filter check a `gate_locked=True` flag to skip its mutations entirely.
critical_code_review_comments: The B3 gate has now had 3 layered root causes across 3 rounds, all in different files, and Round 3 revealed a 4th layer: the voice/path-mangling filter itself corrupts file paths in the gate output. The current architecture has too many mutually-visible content-mutating passes — recommend a single 'final content freeze' point with an immutable flag, downstream filters must check and skip.
chat/stream emits `{type:step, done:true}` intermediate frames which is a footgun for any SSE consumer treating done:true as terminal.
The B3 gate flakes (1/3 hit rate on stream) suggests it may depend on state populated by an async worker that hasn't finished when the stream router reads it. Needs an await/sync point.

rca of the issue: Two distinct failures in this round: (1) On both chat/stream (2/3 runs) and chat/send (this round), the file path in the required_read_gate's canonical output is being corrupted by the business_voice_filter / path-mangling filter running AFTER the gate — outputs contain `.that page` / `a project page` / `website` instead of the actual file path. (2) Additionally on chat/stream 2/3 runs, the LLM-generated response is streaming through instead of the canonical gate replacement — suggesting enforce_required_read_gate() is not always firing, likely because state.required_read_gate stashed by worker.py is being read before it's populated in the async worker, OR the pre-LLM classifier is non-deterministically failing to tag the prompt. Mitigation: (a) exempt file-path tokens from the mangling filter, (b) add an immutable content freeze flag after enforce_required_read_gate() that downstream filters must respect, (c) add an await/sync barrier between worker stash and stream.py's read of state.required_read_gate, (d) log both `pre.get('required_read_gate')` at worker time and `state.required_read_gate` at stream-guard time so the flake can be diagnosed.
